new.title: Recommended

types.PEA: EU-listed stocks and ETFs. €150,000 cap, income-tax exemption after 5 years.
types.CTO: Unlimited universe, no cap. 31.4% flat tax on gains.
types.LIVRET_A: Regulated savings: deposits capped at €22,950 (only interest may exceed), 1.7% rate, tax-free. No positions.
types.PRIV: Private equity / ELTIF (e.g. Apollo, EQT Nexus at Trade Republic). Evergreen funds, 2-4.5% annual fees, quarterly liquidity.

new.privTax: Standard tax treatment — 31.4% flat tax on gains, no PEA-style advantage. Evergreen funds (ELTIF) allow monthly subscriptions but redemption is generally only possible once a quarter, with notice.
new.privFees: Watch the fees: ~2-3%/year management + broker rebate, sometimes a performance fee. Expect 3-4.5%/year all-in, compared with ~0.2% for a world ETF. Valuation (NAV) is monthly and smoothed: displayed volatility understates the real risk. Consider it a long-term diversification complement, in a small share of your wealth.

livretBadges.taxFree: Interest exempt from income tax and social contributions

new.livretNoPositions: No positions — the account is tracked as a balance: deposits, withdrawals and interest computed per fortnight (capitalised on 31 December). Regular DCA deposits are possible.
new.livretNote: Beyond the €22,950 cap, deposits earn no interest. The current rate (1.7% since 1 August 2026) and the inflation rate are adjustable in the account to estimate the real evolution of your purchasing power.
new.flatTax: 31.4% flat tax = 12.8% income tax + 18.6% social contributions
new.peaAfter5: After 5 years: income-tax exemption, only social contributions (18.6%) remain due on gains. Withdrawing before 5 years closes the plan (except legal cases).
new.ctoNote: Identical tax treatment regardless of holding period. Progressive-scale option available on the annual tax return.

livret.overCapText: Only capitalized interest can push the balance beyond the cap — deposits are blocked there. If this balance exceeds the cap through your historical deposits, the surplus is tracked outside the livret: very low yield, harmful to your savings. Move it to a interest-bearing account (other regulated savings account, euro fund…).

fee.impactDetail: vs same portfolio at 0.15%/yr — 6.2% equity return before fees.

income.excludedAcc: Accumulating ETF — dividend reinvested in the price
income.empty: No position paying a cash dividend — accumulating ETFs (Acc) and non-dividend stocks are excluded.
income.disclaimer: Only cash payments are counted. The projection applies the 2025 yield of the reference file to the current value; frequency comes from actual history or the usual quarterly cycle of US stocks. Gross amounts, before flat tax.

performance.xirrHint: XIRR (money-weighted) finds the rate that reconciles all your deposits with the current value: each contribution is only credited for the time it was actually invested. It answers: what did MY money earn?
performance.twrHint: Time-weighted return removes the effect of your deposits: it is the strategy's own performance, comparable to the ETF's published return.
performance.simpleWhy: The simple return mixes performance with deposit timing: it understates your performance in a rising market (your money was not invested the whole period) and overstates it in a falling one.
performance.referencesHint: Theoretical final value if the same deposits had been invested at the given rate — the world equities historical average stands in for a basic strategy.
performance.verdictPositive: Your portfolio beats the reference strategies: complexity adds return.
performance.verdictWarning: Your portfolio roughly tracks the references: complexity is not adding extra return yet.
performance.verdictNegative: Your portfolio does worse than a basic strategy: complexity is costing you return.
performance.verdictNeutral: Not enough history to draw a verdict yet.
performance.verdictHint: Indicative comparison: XIRR includes the effect of your deposit dates, the reference is a constant rate. If the gap stays negative, simplifying (broad ETF, low fees) is probably better.
performance.disclaimer: Annualized XIRR on real cash flows (deposits), chained TWR on valuations. Minimum period of 30 days. Capitalized dividends are included in the value; cash dividends are not reinvested.

diversification.disclaimer: Look-through: ETFs unfolded according to their reference index breakdown (approximations meant to be replaced by actual holdings).

simulator.extraSavingsHint: adds to the current DCA ({amount}/mo) and goes to investing
simulator.disclaimer: Invested (stocks/ETFs): compounding at the chosen return. Savings (bank accounts): contractual rate {rate}, real deposits of {amount}/mo. The active DCA always goes to investing, never to savings.

etf.terHint: Total Expense Ratio: the fund's total annual costs (management, administration, legal). They are deducted directly from the fund — displayed performance is therefore net of fees.
etf.terSub: deducted from the fund, included in performance
etf.yieldHint: Dividends and coupons paid in cash over 2025, as a percentage of the price. An accumulating ETF automatically reinvests these amounts in the fund (no cash payment).
etf.providerHint: Asset manager running the fund (BlackRock, Amundi, Vanguard…). It decides on replication and fees but does not hold the assets: they are segregated with a depositary.
etf.indexHint: Market benchmark the fund tries to replicate (e.g. MSCI World = ~1,400 large companies from 23 developed countries). Fund performance is compared against this index.
etf.assetClassHint: Type of assets held by the fund: equities, bonds, private equity (unlisted ELTIFs)… Determines expected return and risk.
etf.regionHint: Geographic area covered by the index: World (developed), Europe, Emerging Markets, France… The wider the area, the stronger the diversification.
etf.sectorFocusHint: Economic sectors covered: “All sectors” = every industry (tech, healthcare, finance…). A single focus (e.g. tech only) concentrates risk.
etf.isinHint: International Securities Identification Number: 12 characters (2 country letters + 9 characters + check key). Unique per fund, used across the app to link positions and detail sheets.
etf.tickerHint: Short ticker on the main exchange (e.g. WPEA on Euronext Paris). Easier to remember than the ISIN.
etf.yahooHint: Symbol used to fetch live prices from Yahoo Finance (suffixed by exchange: .PA = Paris, .DE = Xetra).
etf.wknHint: Wertpapierkennnummer: 6-character German identifier, the ISIN equivalent on German-speaking exchanges.
etf.fundCurrencyHint: The fund's accounting currency. Note: even for a USD fund, the EUR share class (hedged) removes currency risk; the USD share (unhedged) is exposed to it.
etf.currencyRiskHint: Unhedged: your return also follows EUR/USD moves (favourable when the dollar rises). Hedged: currency is neutralised, at the cost of a small yield discount.
etf.domicileHint: Country where the fund is legally registered. Ireland and Luxembourg are the most common UCITS domiciles: tax advantage on US dividends (treaty, ~15% instead of 30%).
etf.exchangeHint: Exchange where the share is traded: Euronext Paris, Xetra (Germany), Borsa Italiana… Liquidity is usually best on the dominant exchange.
etf.holdingsCountHint: Number of lines held by the index: ~1,400 for MSCI World. The higher, the better the diversification (any single company carries little weight).
etf.holdingsAsOfHint: Date of the breakdown data (holdings, countries, sectors) published by the issuer — usually the latest monthly or quarterly report.
etf.holdingsEmpty: Holdings list unavailable for this ETF.
etf.holdingsDisclaimer: Weights from the fund's latest report — full breakdowns ({count} holdings) are published by the issuer.
etf.countriesHint: Geographic breakdown of the fund: weight of each country in the ETF portfolio, as published by the issuer.
etf.sectorsHint: Sector breakdown: weight of each industry (tech, healthcare, finance...) in the ETF portfolio.
etf.breakdownEmpty: Geographic and sector breakdown unavailable for this ETF.
etf.breakdownDisclaimer: Fund breakdowns published by the issuer — the first 4 lines are shown, the rest unfolds. These are “look-through” breakdowns: they show the actual basket content (stocks, bonds) held by the ETF, not cascading funds.

action.priceHint: Daily closing price (Yahoo Finance), sampled over about 80 points. The percentage compares the first and last point of the period.
action.marketCapHint: Total market value of the company: price × number of outstanding shares. Above $200bn we talk about mega-caps (Apple, Microsoft...).
action.peHint: P/E ratio: price divided by earnings per share over the trailing 12 months. Around 15-20× on historical average for the US market. A high ratio signals strong expected growth (or an expensive stock).
action.volumeDayHint: Number of shares traded today. High volume means strong liquidity: you buy/sell without moving the price.
action.volume3mHint: Daily average of trades over 3 months: more reliable than today's volume to judge the structural liquidity of the stock.
action.high52Hint: Highest price over the past year. Acts as psychological resistance: approaching it can trigger profit-taking.
action.low52Hint: Lowest price over the past year. Close to the low = potentially undervalued, but often for a reason (deteriorating earnings).
action.ma50Hint: Moving average of the last 50 sessions (~2.5 months): short-term trend indicator. Price above = recent positive momentum.
action.ma200Hint: Moving average of the last 200 sessions (~10 months): long-term reference for institutional investors. Price above = secular uptrend.
action.dividendYieldHint: Annual dividend ÷ current price. This is the cash income the stock pays out each year, as a percentage of your investment. 2 to 4% is common for a mature company.
action.dividendRateHint: Total amount distributed per share over the trailing 12 months. A company raising it regularly signals recurring earnings.
action.payoutHint: Share of net profit paid out as dividends. Below 60% is sustainable (the company keeps money to invest); above 100% is a warning sign (it pays more than it earns).
action.priceToBookHint: Market capitalisation ÷ book value of assets. Useful for banks/industries: below 1 means the market values the company below its net assets.
action.betaHint: Sensitivity of the stock to the market: 1 = moves like the market, < 1 = more stable than the market, > 2 = very jittery. A beta of 2 means ±2% when the market moves ±1%.
action.sectorHint: Broad economic family (Technology, Healthcare, Energy…). Diversifying across sectors reduces cyclical risk: each sector reacts differently to the economic cycle.
action.industryHint: Precise sub-segment of the sector (e.g. Semiconductors within Technology). Two companies in the same sector can behave very differently depending on their industry.
action.employeesHint: Full-time headcount. Shows the company's scale: revenue per employee (revenue ÷ headcount) is a good productivity indicator.
action.listingCurrencyHint: Currency the stock is quoted in. If it differs from EUR (USD, CHF…), your real return includes the currency move between purchase and sale.
action.tickerHint: Short ticker symbol (e.g. NVDA). Watch out for collisions: two companies can share a ticker on different exchanges.
action.yahooHint: Symbol used to fetch live prices from Yahoo Finance (suffixed by exchange: .PA = Paris, .SW = Switzerland, .KS = Korea…).
action.isinHint: Unique 12-character international identifier (2 country letters + 9 characters + check key). The only reliable identifier across all exchanges.
action.exchangeHint: Exchange where the stock is traded (NASDAQ, NYSE, Euronext…). Trading hours and dividend taxation depend on the exchange.
